articles.title: Dreamforce 2026: Slack's newest innovations turn AI into a true teammate
articles.summary: Slack is expanding far beyond chat with Slackbot in channels, full-screen AI workspaces, live Salesforce-powered Surfaces, and Slack Code, where developers and AI agents can build and review code collaboratively. Slack is becoming a control surface for more business systems and agents, raising new questions around app governance, permissions, licensing, and what employees should be allowed to connect.

articles.title: Windows 11 KB5129195 is out after Microsoft confirms major issues with the September 2026 update, but it won't fix AMD GPU errors
articles.summary: Microsoft has released an out-of-band Windows 11 update after September's Patch Tuesday caused problems with Remote Desktop, audio, virtualized apps, and other components. KB5129195 fixes several of the issues, but reported Explorer crashes, File History failures, some USB audio problems, and AMD GPU instability remain worth watching before accelerating enterprise deployment.

articles.title: AI Was Supposed to Make Software Cheaper. So Why Is It More Expensive Now?
articles.summary: Despite dramatic improvements in developer productivity and falling unit costs for AI intelligence, software is becoming more expensive due to rising software scope and Jevons paradox driving up consumption. Software has historically been priced on the value delivered to the buyer rather than production labor costs. Consequently, efficiency gains are absorbed by increased inference usage and higher feature expectations rather than lower bills.

articles.title: Dreamforce opens with AI, but questions for CIOs remain
articles.summary: Salesforce's Dreamforce announcements point toward enterprise software being accessed increasingly through agents, MCP, and conversational interfaces rather than traditional application screens. The unresolved IT question is economic: as software moves away from predictable seat-based licensing toward agent usage, MCP calls, and consumption pricing, CIOs may gain flexibility while losing some cost predictability.

articles.title: When Your CRM Starts Building Itself: The CIO's Role in the Agentic SaaS Era
articles.summary: AI is turning business users into application and agent builders faster than traditional IT processes can keep up. Instead of trying to centrally build everything, CIOs increasingly need to own the foundations - identity, data architecture, observability, integration standards, and agent governance - while letting business teams build safely on top of them.

articles.title: Meet Adapt, Westpac's Azure-based enterprise data platform
articles.summary: Westpac's Adapt is a new enterprise data platform built on Microsoft Azure that consolidates data from 285 source systems into a single governed environment. The platform required migrating over 1PB of data and 14,000 data pipelines. Additionally, Westpac utilizes a Snowflake-powered intelligence layer to run advanced AI models on data at rest without moving it.

articles.title: Zoom unveils AI-powered revenue OS to unify buyer intelligence, customer conversations, and revenue execution
articles.summary: Zoom is expanding its platform with Common Room integration and new Revenue Accelerator capabilities for engagement and forecasting. It is another example of collaboration vendors broadening into adjacent enterprise workflows, potentially giving IT teams more opportunities to consolidate tools, but also more overlap to evaluate across CRM, meeting intelligence, and sales platforms.

articles.title: Introducing Builder Central: The No Code AI Workspace for Salesforce
articles.summary: Salesforce Builder Central is a no-code AI workspace designed to let admins and business users build and configure apps and agents using plain language. Powered by Headless Toolkit, the workspace natively reads company metadata and Data 360 context while providing built-in trust, security, and automatic safety checks. The beta version is scheduled to launch the week of September 21.

articles.title: Build with Confidence: App Governance, Access, and Accountability at HubSpot
articles.summary: HubSpot is adding centralized controls for which apps and AI connectors can be installed, who can install them, what data they can access, and who owns each integration. Particularly useful for IT: admins can require approval, use more granular OAuth scopes, restrict MCP access to company-provisioned accounts, see app activity logs, and get warned when deactivating someone who owns an integration.

articles.title: Obsidian Vault to Enterprise Company Brain: Where Agents Write, Branch, and Merge
articles.summary: Scaling knowledge management from a personal Obsidian graph to an enterprise-grade "company brain" requires AI agents to manage knowledge without corrupting it through hallucinations or conflicting updates. Versioned branches, object storage, and a typed graph schema can keep changes controlled, with human review governing merges.

articles.title: AI cloud bills are forcing technology leaders to rethink AWS, Azure and GCP commitments
articles.summary: AI workloads are disrupting traditional cloud commitments as GPU availability, data movement, egress fees, and unpredictable inference demand make long-term AWS, Azure, and GCP agreements harder to forecast. CIOs are increasingly separating AI infrastructure economics from general cloud spend, negotiating more flexible capacity terms, and deciding which high-cost workloads need to remain portable across providers

articles.title: Microsoft Teams: External presenters can manage event production controls
articles.summary: Teams organizers can give trusted B2B and guest presenters production controls for events, reducing the need to provision external event-production partners as internal users.

articles.title: Scaling Claude with Cost Controls (45 minute video)
articles.summary: Anthropic walks admins through new Claude Enterprise controls for model defaults, per-user spend visibility, usage reporting, and managing consumption-based AI costs without a dedicated FinOps operation.

articles.title: More JFrog Artifactory Bugs Are Under Attack, and All Three Have Patches
articles.summary: Researchers at Wiz report active exploitation of three JFrog Artifactory vulnerabilities, including an authentication-bypass bug and two flaws being chained together for privilege escalation.
